title: `regexp` and the cost of a regular expression

videos.script: A regular expression is a small program for recognising text. This lesson writes a few, and then measures them. {{match}} First, finding, extracting and rewriting, over three lines of a server log. Three digits finds one hundred and four, inside an order number. A word boundary fixes it. Named groups pull out the status and the path. {{re2}} Then the engine itself. Go's regexp refuses two features other languages have, and the reason is a promise: time in proportion to the text. You watch one pattern take Python two seconds on twenty-seven characters, and Go a microsecond. {{cost}} Last, the costs that remain. Compiling inside a loop costs thirty-five times as much as compiling once. And a question two string functions can answer is faster still without a pattern. {{close}} Lesson 24 puts files inside the binary itself, with go:embed.
